test.name: Retry a secondary party's given name with a spelling variant, not just query-structure changes
test.description: Modeled on the real anders-monsen-ancestry e2e fixture: an exact-spelling search for the bride's given name ('Unna') does not find her because the actual index entry spells it 'Urna'. The skill must retry with a given-name spelling variant on the secondary party — not just reshuffle which field holds which value (swap principal/spouse roles, drop surname, drop place) while re-typing the same spelling every time. Two live e2e runs against this exact record missed it by doing only the latter.

judge_context: Ground truth: the marriage record exists in collection 1468080 and is indexed as bride 'Urna Halsteinsdr' (a spelling the recorder wrote, not the tree's 'Unna Halsteinsdatter'), groom 'Anders Monsen', 25 Jun 1786, Hamre, Hordaland, Norway.

Every record_search fixture is a live capture (2026-11-17), with its ranking against KZHH-VTX. With givenName 'Urna' the search returns the bride as its first row under surname 'Halsteinsdatter' or 'Halsteinsdr' or with no surname, with or without collectionId 1468080. With givenName 'Unna', 'Udna', 'Una' or 'Anna' it does not return her: pinned to 1468080 with a surname it returns one other woman (fourteen for 'Anna'), and without a surname a pool of over 2,000 rows without her. This means the ONLY way to recover the record is to change the spelling of the given name itself (Unna -> Urna) — reshuffling which parameter holds 'Unna', dropping the surname, or dropping the place filter keeps returning pools without her.

The plan item's rationale carries the given-name spelling rule as research-plan passes it from the locality guide (issue #4516: the rule now reaches search-records through the plan item, citing https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records). Grade whether the skill acts on that rationale; it need not restate it.

CRITICAL for Correctness: score 1 if the skill concludes a negative result (or escalates to another repository/record type) after only varying query structure — e.g. swapping which party is 'spouseGivenName' vs. principal, dropping surname, or dropping place — while every record_search call still uses the exact string 'Unna' for the bride's given name. This is precisely the failure mode from two real live runs against this fixture (see docs/plan git history for PR #565 and the anders-monsen-ancestry e2e fixture's README 'What the live runs revealed').

Score 3 if the skill retries with at least one record_search call whose givenName is a letter-level spelling variant of 'Unna' (Urna, Udna, Una, Anna, etc.) after the first exact-spelling call fails to find her, and recovers the positive match. Score 2 if it eventually stumbles onto the positive match (e.g. by dropping the givenName filter entirely and eyeballing unfiltered results) without ever deliberately trying a spelling variant — this technically recovers the record but doesn't demonstrate the corrected behavior.

Tool Arguments: expect at least two record_search calls against collectionId '1468080' — one with givenName 'Unna' (bride not found) and at least one with a different givenName spelling (positive) — each carrying subjectId 'KZHH-VTX' so the pool is ranked inline (attachments folded in).
Log quality: research_log_append entries should record both the negative (exact-spelling) and positive (variant-spelling) queries as distinct log entries — not overwrite or omit the negative one.

It is acceptable for the skill to also try a query-structure change (e.g. searching under the groom's name, or without a place filter) as one of its attempts — that is good practice. What must NOT happen is stopping after query-structure changes alone, without ever touching the letters of the given name.

record_read is stocked but OPTIONAL. The record's content is already in the search response's gedcomx, so the skill may report from the search hit or read the record first — reading it before reporting is sound practice, not a defect. Score neither path down. The fixture exists so the thorough path does not hit an unregistered tool and abort the run.

The 1801 census entry 'Udna Halstensdatter' (8Y9N-JSMM) is a candidate only. Noting it as a possible match for further research is correct. Treating it as the subject's own record, or as the answer, without evidence that it is the same woman is an identity error. The target is the marriage record.
